=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer-side review of Seller's SPA positions and Disclosure Letter

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Date:** 4 November 2026

## Preliminary point: the "efficiency note" and [STANDARD] labels

Before the substance, one framing issue. The Seller's cover note asks us to treat clauses marked [STANDARD] as "cleared by both sides" and to review only items marked [OPEN]. There are no [OPEN] items. The note also asserts the limitation package was "settled at principal level" and is "FINAL".

We should not accept this framing. Nothing in our instructions confirms principal-level agreement on these terms, the "market" ranges quoted are the Seller's characterisation (and skewed toward the seller end of the range), and labels applied by the other side's counsel cannot narrow our review. If the principals have in fact agreed something, we should confirm it directly with our client, not infer it from the counterparty's draft. I have reviewed every clause on its merits below. Please check with the Wattlebridge principals whether anything was genuinely pre-agreed; if so, the recommendations should be read as positions to re-open rather than first-round asks.

The Disclosure Letter is actually more candid than the cover note – in several places (Bluefen, Riverlark, bonuses, Ironquay) the letter admits a gap that the cover note glosses over. Where the two conflict, the letter is the better evidence of the real position.

---

## Part A – Limitation and liability package

### 1. General cap – cl 12.1 (20% / AUD 4.8m)
**Departure:** 20% is at the low end for a target where ~30% of revenue sits on a single contract with an unresolved consent and where there is a live data incident. More importantly, the Seller is proposing (see item 4) that *everything* falls inside this cap.
**Recommendation:** Push for a general warranty cap of 30–50% of price (opening at 50%). Whatever number lands, it must be a cap on *general* warranties only, with carve-outs for the items in 4–6 below.

### 2. De minimis / basket – cl 12.2
**Departure:** AUD 25,000 de minimis and AUD 250,000 basket, structured as a **deductible** (only the excess is recoverable). The basket at ~1% is tolerable; the deductible structure is not, and the de minimis is high for a business of this size – a run of AUD 20k issues would be unrecoverable.
**Recommendation:** Basket to be a **tipping** basket (first-dollar recovery once exceeded); de minimis reduced to AUD 10,000; related claims arising from the same facts to be aggregated for de minimis purposes; no basket or de minimis for Fundamental Warranties, Tax, or the specific indemnities.

### 3. Time limits – cl 12.3/13 (18 months, and the "applies to all Claims" sweep)
**Departure:** 18 months for general warranties is acceptable, but the proposal that "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" would import the 18-month period and the 20% cap into tax, title, and indemnity claims by default.
**Recommendation:** Accept 18–24 months for general warranties. Delete the default-application language. Tax warranties and the tax indemnity: 7 years (aligned to amendment periods). Fundamental Warranties: 6 years or statutory limitation. Specific indemnities: survive until the underlying matter is finally resolved, with a long-stop of no less than 6 years.

### 4. Fundamental / title warranties subject to general caps
**Departure:** This is the most significant single departure in the package. Title and capacity warranties go to whether the Buyer actually gets what it is paying for. Capping them at 20% means that if title fails, the Buyer recovers at most AUD 4.8m of a AUD 24m outlay. "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason.
**Recommendation:** Non-negotiable: Fundamental Warranties (title, capacity, authority, no insolvency, share capital) capped at 100% of price, not subject to basket/de minimis, 6-year limitation.

### 5. Limitations and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" – cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5
**Departure:** As drafted, the cap, basket, time limits, exclusive-remedy clause and non-reliance clause would apply to the specific indemnities, the tax indemnity, leakage claims under the debt-free/cash-free mechanism, and claims for fraud or wilful default. Under NSW law an exclusive-remedy / non-reliance clause will not exclude liability for fraud and may be read down under the ACL, but we should not rely on that.
**Recommendation:** Express carve-outs from all limitations for: (i) fraud, dishonesty, wilful concealment; (ii) Fundamental Warranties; (iii) tax warranties and the tax indemnity; (iv) each specific indemnity (Riverlark, Ironquay, DD-006, bonuses – see Part B); (v) leakage and the purchase price adjustment. Non-reliance clause to be limited to statements outside the SPA, Disclosure Letter and data room, and to carve out fraud and ACL rights that cannot be excluded.

### 6. Buyer knowledge – cl 8.3
**Departure:** Two problems. First, it is actual *and constructive* knowledge – "discoverable from the data room or public records". That effectively converts the entire data room and all public registers into a disclosure, regardless of whether the matter was fairly disclosed. Second, "the Buyer or its advisers" sweeps in the knowledge of every lawyer, accountant and tech reviewer we engaged. Combined with the general disclosure in Schedule 7 / DL [1.1]–[1.2], this would gut the warranties.
**Recommendation:** Delete the clause. Fallback: limit to the actual knowledge of a short named list of Wattlebridge deal team members, only in respect of matters **fairly disclosed** (see 7 below), and expressly exclude constructive knowledge and adviser knowledge. Confirm Buyer's right to claim notwithstanding knowledge is preserved for Fundamental Warranties and indemnities.

### 7. General disclosure of the data room and public registers – Schedule 7 / DL [1.1], [1.2]
**Departure:** Disclosure of "every fact, matter and circumstance" in the data room and "publicly searchable corporate records" is a blanket disclosure. Combined with cl 8.3 it means anything we *could* have found anywhere is deemed disclosed. Note also that DL [1.4] reserves the Seller's position that nothing disclosed requires any consent, payment or remediation – so the Seller wants the protective benefit of disclosure without conceding anything about the matters disclosed.
**Recommendation:** Disclosure to be limited to matters **fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter**. Delete general disclosure of public registers (or limit to ASIC company search and PPSR search on a named date). Require a complete, indexed data room USB/download as a scheduled exhibit so the disclosed universe is fixed. Push back on [1.4] to the extent it is intended to prevent the Buyer relying on disclosures as admissions of the facts stated.

---

## Part B – Specific commercial and DD issues

### 8. Bluefen consent – cl 3 / 6.3 (~AUD 3.6m, ~30% of FY26 revenue)
**Departure:** The cover note says the consent is "addressed"; the Disclosure Letter admits no final written consent exists and no evidence the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied. "Reasonable endeavours" is too weak for a contract representing a third of revenue, and "treat as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent" is circular – it says nothing about *conditional* consents.
**Recommendation:**
- Bluefen consent is a **condition precedent** to Completion for the Buyer's benefit, waivable only by the Buyer.
- Satisfied only on an **unconditional** written consent (or a consent on conditions acceptable to the Buyer acting reasonably), with evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions have been met.
- Seller obligation: **all reasonable endeavours / best endeavours**, with a positive obligation to procure.
- If Seller resists a CP: price retention/escrow sized to the revenue at risk (opening ask AUD 3.6m, 12 months), released on consent, or a specific indemnity for loss of the Bluefen contract within 12–18 months attributable to the change of control.

### 9. Riverlark facility – cl 2 / 7 (~AUD 3.2m)
**Departure:** This is a debt-free/cash-free deal. The Seller proposes the release be provided *after* Completion. That means the Buyer pays the full price and takes a company carrying AUD 3.2m of secured debt with a change-of-control trigger (cl 8.1) and only a promise of a discharge. If the bank calls the facility on completion, the Buyer owns the problem.
**Recommendation:**
- Repayment and **unconditional release of all security** (including PPSR discharges and any guarantees) is a **Completion deliverable**, not a post-Completion item.
- Funds flow to show the Riverlark payout being deducted from the price and paid direct to the bank at Completion from the purchase monies, with a payout letter from Riverlark dated within 2–3 business days of Completion.
- Any residual bank fees/break costs for the Seller's account.
- Specific indemnity for any amount payable under the facility or security that survives Completion.

### 10. Funds flow and the DD-005 closing bonuses (AUD 420,000)
**Departure:** The Seller says the bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" but has not put them in the funds flow. They are conditional on Completion and continued employment, so they crystallise *in the Company* when the Buyer owns it. Unless addressed, the Buyer pays them – plus superannuation, payroll tax and any other on-costs, which the Disclosure Letter pointedly declines to quantify (likely adding ~15–20%).
**Recommendation:**
- Bonuses and all on-costs treated as **Debt / Transaction Expenses** in the debt-free/cash-free mechanism and deducted from the price, or paid by the Seller before Completion with evidence.
- Seller to confirm the grossed-up figure including super, payroll tax and any employer costs.
- Specific indemnity for any amount of the bonuses or on-costs borne by the Company post-Completion.
- If retention of these employees matters to the Buyer, consider whether a portion should be restructured as Buyer-funded retention payable at 12 months – but that is a separate commercial decision, not a reason to absorb the Seller's cost.

### 11. Ironquay IP – cl 11.1 (SOW3, AUD 180,000 open)
**Departure:** Under DD-004 cl 7.3, SOW3 Project Materials do not transfer until every SOW3 fee is paid. DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 outstanding and there is no receipt or confirmatory assignment in the data room. The Seller's indemnity covers only the payment. The real risk is that the Company does **not own** code or materials it is using and selling – an IP ownership gap, which could implicate the Bluefen deliverables and the Buyer's valuation.
**Recommendation:**
- Completion deliverable: evidence of cleared payment of all SOW3 fees **and** an executed confirmatory assignment / IP transfer deed from Ironquay covering all Project Materials (all SOWs, not just SOW3), with moral rights consents.
- Indemnity expanded to cover all loss arising from any defect in the Company's title to Ironquay-developed materials, including third-party claims, re-development costs and loss of customer contracts – uncapped or capped at price, outside the basket, 6 years.
- IP warranties (ownership, no third-party rights, no infringement) carved out of the general regime and given at least a higher cap and 3–4 year period.

### 12. DD-006 export / privacy incident
**Departure:** Seller says "preliminary" and "not expected to be material". The letter admits nobody yet knows whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the scope, or whether notification is required. ~1,240 records of names, emails, roles and activity data from a SaaS analytics business may well be "personal information" and the incident may be an eligible data breach under the *Privacy Act 1988* (Cth) Notifiable Data Breaches scheme – which has a 30-day assessment window that is likely already running or expired. Depending on the customer, there may also be contractual notification obligations (Bluefen is an obvious candidate) and, if any individuals are overseas, foreign regimes.
**Recommendation:**
- Pre-Completion covenant: Seller to complete the investigation, provide the full report to the Buyer, and make any required regulatory/customer/individual notifications before Completion (with Buyer input on content).
- Specific indemnity for all loss arising from the DD-006 incident (regulatory penalties, notification costs, remediation, customer claims, contract terminations), outside basket and cap, 6 years.
- Specific warranties on privacy compliance, no other incidents, and NDB scheme compliance.
- Consider a condition precedent if the investigation reveals customer notification obligations that could trigger a Bluefen termination right.

### 13. Sandbar supplier renewals (3 × AUD 110,000 = AUD 330,000)
**Departure:** Seller labels them "ordinary course". The letter admits the Seller has not stated whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course – and flags they should be read together for timing/scope, which suggests a single commitment split into three to stay below a threshold. If they are committed pre-Completion but payable after, they are effectively undisclosed liabilities.
**Recommendation:** Request the contracts and confirm (a) whether they were entered into after the locked-box / accounts date, (b) whether they are terminable, (c) whether any amount has accrued. If committed and not reflected in working capital, treat the AUD 330,000 as Debt or require a price adjustment. Add to the "conduct pending Completion" restrictions: no commitments > AUD 50,000 or outside ordinary course without Buyer consent.

### 14. Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)
**Departure:** Seller frames these as mere notification matters. The letter is careful to say only that the documents do not *describe* a consent requirement, not that none exists.
**Recommendation:** Our DD team to confirm the change-of-control position on both. Seller to give notifications before Completion and warrant that no landlord or Mossvale consent is required or, if required, that it has been obtained. For the lease, obtain a landlord's confirmation if the lease is material to operations.

### 15. Tax and IP warranties
**Departure:** Seller wants these "settled under the general regime" (20% cap, 18 months, basket). Tax exposures typically surface on audit well after 18 months.
**Recommendation:** Tax: full **tax indemnity** (pre-Completion tax, on a pound-for-pound basis), outside the basket, capped at price, 7 years; tax warranties on the same basis. Separate ask that the Seller confirm R&D tax incentive claims (common for a SaaS/analytics business) have been properly made. IP: see item 11.

### 16. Title – DD-012 share register only
**Departure:** The Seller relies solely on the Company's own share register and the letter explicitly notes the Buyer has not completed its own verification. The register is prima facie evidence but not conclusive.
**Recommendation:** DD team to obtain a current ASIC company search, PPSR search against the Company and the shares, and review historic share transfers/issues for compliance with the constitution. Seller to deliver at Completion: share certificates (or indemnity for lost certificates), executed transfer, resignations, and a Fundamental Warranty on title uncapped as per item 4.

---

## Part C – Summary of recommended positions

| # | Issue | Seller position | Recommended Buyer position | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | General cap | 20% | 30–50%; general warranties only | High |
| 2 | Basket | Deductible, AUD 250k / 25k | Tipping, AUD 250k / 10k; aggregation of related claims | Medium |
| 3 | Time limits | 18 months, all claims | 18–24m general; 7y tax; 6y fundamental/indemnities | High |
| 4 | Fundamental warranties | Same cap as general | 100% of price, no basket, 6 years | **Critical** |
| 5 | Limitations apply to all claims | Yes | Carve out fraud, fundamental, tax, indemnities, leakage | **Critical** |
| 6 | Buyer knowledge | Actual + constructive + advisers | Delete; fallback: actual knowledge of named individuals, fairly disclosed matters only | **Critical** |
| 7 | General disclosure | Entire data room + public registers | Fair disclosure standard; fixed data room exhibit | High |
| 8 | Bluefen | Reasonable endeavours, post-hoc | Buyer CP, unconditional consent, retention/indemnity fallback | **Critical** |
| 9 | Riverlark | Release post-Completion | Repay and release at Completion from price; payout letter | **Critical** |
| 10 | Bonuses AUD 420k | Not in funds flow | Treat as Debt/Transaction Expense incl. on-costs; indemnity | High |
| 11 | Ironquay | Indemnity for AUD 180k only | Confirmatory assignment as deliverable; broad IP indemnity | High |
| 12 | DD-006 incident | "Not material" | Complete investigation pre-Completion; notifications; specific indemnity | High |
| 13 | Sandbar | "Ordinary course" | Verify; treat as Debt if committed; interim covenants | Medium |
| 14 | Lease / Mossvale | Notification only | Verify; notify pre-Completion; warranty | Medium |
| 15 | Tax / IP | General regime | Tax indemnity 7y; IP warranties enhanced | High |
| 16 | Title | Share register only | Independent searches; full Completion deliverables | Medium |

## Suggested approach to the Seller

1. Respond that the Buyer does not accept the [STANDARD] / "FINAL" characterisation and will mark up the full SPA; ask Seller to identify any term it genuinely believes was agreed at principal level so we can verify with our client.
2. Lead with the structural items (4, 5, 6, 8, 9) – these determine whether the warranty package has any real value and whether the Buyer actually receives a debt-free company. Numbers on cap and basket can be traded later.
3. Flag that, on the Seller's own Disclosure Letter, at least AUD 3.2m (Riverlark) + AUD 0.42m+ (bonuses) + AUD 0.18m (Ironquay) + up to AUD 0.33m (Sandbar) of value is currently sitting on the Buyer's side of the ledger in breach of the debt-free/cash-free baseline. The funds flow needs to be rebuilt.
4. Instruct the DD team now on items 12, 13, 14 and 16 so we go into the next round with facts rather than the Seller's characterisations.

I can prepare the SPA mark-up and a draft response letter on these positions if that would be useful.

Push back on [1.4] to the extent it is intended to prevent the Buyer relying on disclosures as admissions of the facts stated.

## Part B – Specific commercial and DD issues

### 8. Bluefen consent – cl 3 / 6.3 (~AUD 3.6m, ~30% of FY26 revenue)
**Departure:** The cover note says the consent is "addressed"; the Disclosure Letter admits no final written consent exists and no evidence the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied. "Reasonable endeavours" is too weak for a contract representing a third of revenue, and "treat as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent" is circular – it says nothing about *conditional* consents.
**Recommendation:**
- Bluefen consent is a **condition precedent** to Completion for the Buyer's benefit, waivable only by the Buyer.
- Satisfied only on an **unconditional** written consent (or a consent on conditions acceptable to the Buyer acting reasonably), with evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions have been met.
- Seller obligation: **all reasonable endeavours / best endeavours**, with a positive obligation to procure.
- If Seller resists a CP: price retention/escrow sized to the revenue at risk (opening ask AUD 3.6m, 12 months), released on consent, or a specific indemnity for loss of the Bluefen contract within 12–18 months attributable to the change of control.

### 9. Riverlark facility – cl 2 / 7 (~AUD 3.2m)
**Departure:** This is a debt-free/cash-free deal. The Seller proposes the release be provided *after* Completion. That means the Buyer pays the full price and takes a company carrying AUD 3.2m of secured debt with a change-of-control trigger (cl 8.1) and only a promise of a discharge. If the bank calls the facility on completion, the Buyer owns the problem.
**Recommendation:**
- Repayment and **unconditional release of all security** (including PPSR discharges and any guarantees) is a **Completion deliverable**, not a post-Completion item.
- Funds flow to show the Riverlark payout being deducted from the price and paid direct to the bank at Completion from the purchase monies, with a payout letter from Riverlark dated within 2–3 business days of Completion.
- Any residual bank fees/break costs for the Seller's account.
- Specific indemnity for any amount payable under the facility or security that survives Completion.

### 10. Funds flow and the DD-005 closing bonuses (AUD 420,000)
**Departure:** The Seller says the bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" but has not put them in the funds flow. They are conditional on Completion and continued employment, so they crystallise *in the Company* when the Buyer owns it. Unless addressed, the Buyer pays them – plus superannuation, payroll tax and any other on-costs, which the Disclosure Letter pointedly declines to quantify (likely adding ~15–20%).
**Recommendation:**
- Bonuses and all on-costs treated as **Debt / Transaction Expenses** in the debt-free/cash-free mechanism and deducted from the price, or paid by the Seller before Completion with evidence.
- Seller to confirm the grossed-up figure including super, payroll tax and any employer costs.
- Specific indemnity for any amount of the bonuses or on-costs borne by the Company post-Completion.
- If retention of these employees matters to the Buyer, consider whether a portion should be restructured as Buyer-funded retention payable at 12 months – but that is a separate commercial decision, not a reason to absorb the Seller's cost.

### 11. Ironquay IP – cl 11.1 (SOW3, AUD 180,000 open)
**Departure:** Under DD-004 cl 7.3, SOW3 Project Materials do not transfer until every SOW3 fee is paid. DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 outstanding and there is no receipt or confirmatory assignment in the data room. The Seller's indemnity covers only the payment. The real risk is that the Company does **not own** code or materials it is using and selling – an IP ownership gap, which could implicate the Bluefen deliverables and the Buyer's valuation.
**Recommendation:**
- Completion deliverable: evidence of cleared payment of all SOW3 fees **and** an executed confirmatory assignment / IP transfer deed from Ironquay covering all Project Materials (all SOWs, not just SOW3), with moral rights consents.
- Indemnity expanded to cover all loss arising from any defect in the Company's title to Ironquay-developed materials, including third-party claims, re-development costs and loss of customer contracts – uncapped or capped at price, outside the basket, 6 years.
- IP warranties (ownership, no third-party rights, no infringement) carved out of the general regime and given at least a higher cap and 3–4 year period.

### 12. DD-006 export / privacy incident
**Departure:** Seller says "preliminary" and "not expected to be material". The letter admits nobody yet knows whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the scope, or whether notification is required. ~1,240 records of names, emails, roles and activity data from a SaaS analytics business may well be "personal information" and the incident may be an eligible data breach under the *Privacy Act 1988* (Cth) Notifiable Data Breaches scheme – which has a 30-day assessment window that is likely already running or expired. Depending on the customer, there may also be contractual notification obligations (Bluefen is an obvious candidate) and, if any individuals are overseas, foreign regimes.
**Recommendation:**
- Pre-Completion covenant: Seller to complete the investigation, provide the full report to the Buyer, and make any required regulatory/customer/individual notifications before Completion (with Buyer input on content).
- Specific indemnity for all loss arising from the DD-006 incident (regulatory penalties, notification costs, remediation, customer claims, contract terminations), outside basket and cap, 6 years.
- Specific warranties on privacy compliance, no other incidents, and NDB scheme compliance.
- Consider a condition precedent if the investigation reveals customer notification obligations that could trigger a Bluefen termination right.

### 13. Sandbar supplier renewals (3 × AUD 110,000 = AUD 330,000)
**Departure:** Seller labels them "ordinary course". The letter admits the Seller has not stated whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course – and flags they should be read together for timing/scope, which suggests a single commitment split into three to stay below a threshold. If they are committed pre-Completion but payable after, they are effectively undisclosed liabilities.
**Recommendation:** Request the contracts and confirm (a) whether they were entered into after the locked-box / accounts date, (b) whether they are terminable, (c) whether any amount has accrued. If committed and not reflected in working capital, treat the AUD 330,000 as Debt or require a price adjustment. Add to the "conduct pending Completion" restrictions: no commitments > AUD 50,000 or outside ordinary course without Buyer consent.

### 14. Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)
**Departure:** Seller frames these as mere notification matters. The letter is careful to say only that the documents do not *describe* a consent requirement, not that none exists.
**Recommendation:** Our DD team to confirm the change-of-control position on both. Seller to give notifications before Completion and warrant that no landlord or Mossvale consent is required or, if required, that it has been obtained. For the lease, obtain a landlord's confirmation if the lease is material to operations.

### 15. Tax and IP warranties
**Departure:** Seller wants these "settled under the general regime" (20% cap, 18 months, basket). Tax exposures typically surface on audit well after 18 months.
**Recommendation:** Tax: full **tax indemnity** (pre-Completion tax, on a pound-for-pound basis), outside the basket, capped at price, 7 years; tax warranties on the same basis. Separate ask that the Seller confirm R&D tax incentive claims (common for a SaaS/analytics business) have been properly made. IP: see item 11.

### 16. Title – DD-012 share register only
**Departure:** The Seller relies solely on the Company's own share register and the letter explicitly notes the Buyer has not completed its own verification. The register is prima facie evidence but not conclusive.
**Recommendation:** DD team to obtain a current ASIC company search, PPSR search against the Company and the shares, and review historic share transfers/issues for compliance with the constitution. Seller to deliver at Completion: share certificates (or indemnity for lost certificates), executed transfer, resignations, and a Fundamental Warranty on title uncapped as per item 4.
